caption: What if the internet vanished for a day? No reels, no chats, no video calls. UPI handles about 82 crore payments a day in India (a record in October 2026), so the QR code at your chai stall becomes a sticker and cash is king again. Surprise: GPS still works, because satellites only broadcast and your phone just listens. So where does the internet live? Mostly on the seafloor. Undersea cables carry over 99% of data between continents: 600+ cable systems, over 1.5 million km, enough to wrap Earth about 37 times. Most of a cable is only as thick as a garden hose, with glass fibres thin as a hair. Around 200 faults happen every year, mostly from fishing gear and ship anchors. Shark bites are super rare. Plot twist: the first internet message, on 29 October 1969, was meant to say LOGIN. It crashed after just LO. What would YOU do first without internet? 👇
